reading.title: The Canyon Hike
reading.purpose: Hike a dry canyon with Amir and his aunt and notice what is scarce and what is not.
paras: Amir and his aunt Samira started early to hike a dry canyon trail. Samira had packed sufficient water for the whole day, and Amir carried the snacks. "In the desert, you never want a meager supply," she said. "It is better to have too much than too little."
The trail was rocky and bright. Trees were sparse, and the only shade came from tall rocks standing far apart. Amir rarely asked to rest, but today he wanted a break every few minutes.

Lizards darted across the path again and again. "They are frequent visitors here," said Samira. "They love warm rocks." An occasional cloud drifted overhead, but it never brought rain, and the continual buzz of insects followed them up the trail.

At noon they reached a pool where the canyon walls met the sand. Water was plentiful here, because a spring fed the pool all year. Cottonwood trees grew along the edge, and their leaves gave ample shade, enough for the picnic with room to spare.
After lunch, Amir looked up into the branches. Countless leaves shook in the breeze, more than anyone could count. "The desert is full of surprises," he said, and he stood up, ready to hike home.

choices: thick and close together, with little open ground
tall and full of leaves, with deep shade below
spread out thinly, with big gaps
dry and easy to burn when the sun is hot
qs.why: The shade came from rocks "standing far apart," so sparse trees are spread out with big gaps.

qs.q: Which sentence shows that the pool had water all year?
choices: At noon they reached a pool where the canyon walls met the sand.
Water was plentiful here, because a spring fed the pool all year.
Cottonwood trees grew along the edge, and their leaves gave ample shade, enough for the picnic with room to spare.
After lunch, Amir looked up into the branches.
qs.why: A spring that feeds the pool all year is the proof that the water never runs out.

ev.text: Water was plentiful here, because a spring fed the pool all year.

qs.q: Why did Amir want a break every few minutes?
choices: The sun was bright and there was very little shade.
He was bored by the quiet trail and wanted to turn back.
His bag of snacks was too heavy for him to carry.
He had already finished all of the water in his bottle.
qs.why: The trail was bright and trees were sparse, so the only shade was far away, which made walking tiring.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: A family looks for a lost lizard in a rocky and dry canyon.
A girl learns how to build a shelter out of cottonwood leaves.
A boy gets lost in the canyon after running out of his water.
A hike through a dry canyon with little water and shade.
qs.why: The story follows a hike where water and shade are scarce until the pool at noon.

clues.text: darted across the path again and again
a spring fed the pool all year
enough for the picnic with room to spare
